title: General Statement Regarding a Multisig Business Account
intro: A company can use a shared blockchain account involving multiple authorized individuals. Typically, at least three Signer are involved, such as the management, the finance officer, and the compliance/backup representative. The goal is to enable individual persons to execute payments independently without any single person being able to control or take over the account on their own.
problem: If a Signer has enough weight to execute payments and, at the same time, enough weight to make account changes, that person could remove other Signers or adjust the Threshold/weighting (Thresholds), thereby taking control of the account. Conversely, the original owner should not be able to simply exclude other Signer without cross-checking. A multi-sig structure ensures that important decisions are always made jointly by multiple people.
setupTitle: Example of a secure multi-signature structure with three signers
setupWeights:
In an example with three roles of equal standing, all are assigned the same signature strength:
- Signer A (Management): Weight 2
- Signer B (Finanzen): Weight 2
- Signer C (Compliance/Backup): Weight 2
setupThresholds:
To do this, set the appropriate Thresholds/weights:
- Low (low_threshold): 1
- Medium (med_threshold): 2 (for payments and other medium-level actions)
- High (high_threshold): 4 (for structural changes such as adding/removing Signer or changing the Threshold/weighting (Thresholds))
This allows each authorized person to make payments, but no single person can change the account structure on their own.
behavior: With this configuration, payments can be made by any one of the three authorized individuals acting alone, because the individual weight in each case meets the average Threshold/weighting. However, for structural changes such as removing a Signers, adjusting the Thresholds/weights, or merging or closing the account, the high Threshold/weighting (high_threshold). This value can only be achieved if at least two of the three Signer sign jointly. This ensures that the account remains flexible for everyday use while also being well protected against misuse.
removal: If a person leaves the company or is no longer considered trustworthy, any two of the remaining Signer can jointly revoke that person’s signing rights. No single Signer—whether an employee or a member of management—can independently remove others from the account. The revocation of permissions is therefore always carried out in a controlled and traceable manner by at least two authorized individuals.
summary: This type of multi-signature structure allows individual persons to process payments efficiently while the control over the account remains with multiple parties. It reduces the risk of account takeovers, protects against unilateral decisions, and is particularly suitable for corporate accounts where both security and operational flexibility are important.
